entities.summary: Christopher Middleton was a British navigator and Royal Navy officer who played a crucial role in the exploration and mapping of North America during the early 18th century. Born into a family of modest means, Middleton joined the Hudson's Bay Company and later the Royal Navy, where he served under Admiral Edward Vernon. In 1737, he was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society, a prestigious honor that recognized his contributions to the field of navigation and cartography. Middleton's work helped to establish the boundaries of British North America, and his maps played a key role in the company's expansion into the region. He died on February 12, 1770, at the age of 58, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most important navigators of his time. Middleton's work also had a lasting impact on the development of the Royal Navy, and his maps remain an important part of the company's archives. His story is a testament to the power of exploration and the importance of accurate mapping in shaping the course of human history. Middleton's navigational skills and cartographic expertise were unmatched during his time, and his contributions to the field of navigation continue to inspire and inform scholars and historians today.
